newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - JAN 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - JAN 14.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--The day after Sunday's flash flooding found the country with six dead and enormous damage, particularly to the region of Ftiotida. A count of the damage is still pending as the waters have yet to subside but initial estimates put the bill at 40 billion drachmas and possibly more.

--Washington appears satisfied with Cyprus President Glafcos Clerides's commitment that Russian-made S-300 missiles will not be deployed in Cyprus for another 16 months. US State Department official Carey Cavanaugh is in Athens today for talks.

--Greece and Russia agreed to promote their joint interests in the energy sector yesterday, signing a bilateral memorandum that is hoped will assist in realising the development ministry's plans to make Greece a regional energy hub.
--Feverish talks are being conducted in the government in an attempt to stave off further farmers' protests.

--Sources say archaeologists have found a large ancient complex in the heart of Athens that is thought to be the famed Lyceum where Aristotle may have taught. The find was made on the site of works for the Athens Modern Art Museum.
--Civil servants said yesterday they had scheduled a 48-hour strike for February 3.

--Infrastructural reasons were behind the natural disaster to hit Greece on Sunday. In 24 hours on Sunday, five months of rain fell. Half-finished works on Athens' Kifissos Avenue turned the road into a river.
--Archaeologists warn Culture Minister Evangelos Venizelos that the Acropolis "is at the mercy of the gods", as others find evidence of Athens' ancient Lyceum.

--Ruling party PASOK Secretary Costas Skandalidis attacks close associates of Prime Minister Costas Simitis, saying the closed circle are playing with their new-found powers. Skandalidis also called on leading party members to support the prime minister.
--The finance ministry is preparing a new list of tax evaders to be put on file for future cross-reference.
--The government has refused to hand over to the opposition a copy of the audit into Athens Stock Exchange brokerage houses. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
